title: More intuitive and high-performance copying of typed array bytes?
body:
JS applications that require best performance when dealing with large blocks of primitive data will utilize typed arrays (`ArrayBuffer`, `SharedArrayBuffer`) to store and manipulate the data. The WebAssembly standard is also built on top of these primitives.

Developers target WebAssembly often to reach fastest possible runtime speed, and to get a more deterministic execution speed for the program, e.g. when dealing with interactive animation or games.

One of the major enablers of this deterministic worst-case execution speed is that WebAssembly-based programs avoid complex JIT warmup periods, and they do not generate JS garbage, hence suffer from no stuttering pauses from garbage collection.

These applications still regularly need to interact with the JS DOM APIs for some specific execution, which does constitute a source of temporary garbage, depending on the API.

One such place is for doing buffer copies between multiple typed arrays. When dealing with file system data, audio, binary data fetches, or WebGL or WebGPU rendering with buffers and textures, it is common to need to copy the data from/to the WebAssembly memory from an outside ArrayBuffer.

This category of **buffer copying** is one of the simplest and most primitive operations that one can do on a raw block of data (along with the **fill** operation).

Currently, if one has two ArrayBuffers, `src` and `dst`, and wishes to copy some byte sub-region `start` - `end` of bytes from `src` to `dst` to destination offset `dstOffset`, there is no intuitive way to do such a memory block copy. There is no `byteCopy` functionality, but to achieve the task, one needs to learn about two different counterintuitive tricks: 1) developer must realize that copying is achieved instead by the `.set` function of an typed array view, which assigns the contents of one typed array over to another, and 2) the trick is to carefully craft an aliasing temporary typed array view that is sized up exactly to equal the length of the memory copy that is desired.

```js
new Uint8Array(dst).set(new Uint8Array(src, start, end - start), dstOffset);
```

This has the following drawbacks:
- it is not intuitive for the two reasons state above: memory copies are done by assigning an array to another, by first creating a suitable sized aliased view. Nobody thinks about buffer copies that way. The above code line does not look anything like a memory copy.
- it allocates temporary `Uint8Array` objects that creates temp GC pressure in the JS VM
- object allocation needlessly reduces performance from a potentially critical path of the application

I would like to propose that a new member function would be added directly to the `ArrayBuffer` and `SharedArrayBuffer` objects:

```webidl
interface (Shared)ArrayBuffer {
  // Copies the range src[srcOffset]...src[srcOffset+byteLength] over to dst[dstOffset]...dst[dstOffset+byteLength].
  // Returns the number of bytes actually copied. (helpful to detect truncation)
  unsigned long long byteCopy([AllowShared] ArrayBuffer src, unsigned long long srcOffset, unsigned long long byteLength, unsigned long long dstOffset);
};
```

This way, the above type of buffer copy could be performed in a direct intuitive fashion, by typing
```js
dst.byteCopy(src, start, end - start, dstOffset);
```

which would be more self-documenting and performance friendly. Would this kind of addition make sense?
